A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AttrVR research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Pages 2–27 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the first-page differences are identifiable.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original classification experiments, ablations, backbone comparisons, attribute-generation studies, and training-cost measurements.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain the same original empirical results, including classification accuracy, ablations, supplementary experiments, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical attribute generation, sample-specific k-nearest attribute selection, weighted similarity computation, and cross-entropy optimization of visual reprogramming patterns.

E1.justification: The same 12 classification datasets listed in Table 4 and the same test scenarios are used throughout Section 6 and Appendix C.

E2.justification: ZS, AttrZS, VP, and AR retain their participation in the corresponding benchmark comparisons. Comparator membership in the supplementary experiments and control studies is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The splits, 16-shot main evaluation, additional shot counts, CLIP backbones, accuracy metrics, and 200-epoch training protocol remain identical. Appendix experimental settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, hyperparameter analyses in Figure 6, and Appendix C studies of aggregation, cross-testing, computational cost, attribute generators, and attribute quality are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2.3 reports averages over three seeds in both versions. Standard-deviation reporting and plotted error-bar conventions remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same average accuracies of 77.7% for AttrVR and 75.7% for AR under the 16-shot ViT-B16 CLIP setting.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–4, Lemmas 1–2, Corollary 1, and the corresponding proofs in Appendix B are identical. Mathematical assumptions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: Despite broader title wording, the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about AttrVR for CLIP, improved class separability, and performance across 12 tasks. The VLM framing already appears in v1.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations concerning attribute alignment, domain shifts, image-resolution effects, overlapping attribute sets, and low-quality generated attributes. No substantive limitation or qualification changes.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical generation prompts, filtering rules, hyperparameters, and training instructions. Appendix C.5 retains the same hardware and timing details, and the stated code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the substantive positioning relative to visual prompting, model reprogramming, and visual attribute querying are unchanged.

P1.justification: The title ending changes from 'for Image Classification with CLIP' to 'for Vision-Language Models'. Lei Feng's affiliation changes from SUTD to Southeast University and Idealism Technology (Beijing), with an updated email. The arXiv stamp changes; scientific prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–14 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. The first-page text replacements preserve its layout, and pages 2–27 render identically.

improvement.justification: The revision changes the title and author information while retaining identical scientific content, evidence, reproducibility documentation, and supplementary material. These limited editorial updates establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
